utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. We apologise for the delay in commencing this morning. As you can see, Judge Thelin [Realtime transcript read in error "Parker"] is not with us. He is unwell, and in the end it just seemed that it was just not practical for him to sit. So Judge Van den Wyngaert and I will sit under the Rule. May I remind you, sir, that your affirmation still applies. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher provide the witness with the set of documents that is numbered 1. It is the Defence binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: While that's happening, I hope the transcript is not accurate, when it says in line 8 that Judge Parker is not with us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Stojanovski. Do you recall that the Prosecutor on several occasions showed you Article 1 of the Law on Internal Affairs; and, in that regard, he asked you a number of questions, and that was, among others, on page 9246 of the transcript? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, Mr. Stojanovski, how many people are employed in the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 12.000.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All the employees of the Ministry of Interior, do they have their own jobs and work?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The jobs and tasks that they do, are they different types of jobs or are they the same jobs?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They are different types of jobs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Their level of responsibility or the responsibility of the employees, is it identical for all employees or are there different levels of responsibility for the individual employees?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are differences.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, if we take into account all the jobs that these 12000 workers of the Ministry of Interior do, which jobs are they?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that would be listed in Article 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, let's take a look at tab 2 in that same binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is P -- Exhibit P86.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is the Law on Internal Affairs, and I'd like to refer to Article 1 that you looked at together with the Prosecutor during your examination. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We don't have to read it again because you read it out with the Prosecutor. So just tell me whether, in this Article, there is any individual or organ -- or rather, does the Article stress any particular individual to perform these functions stipulated here?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It just provides a general list.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Stojanovski, in view of your experience and the tasks enumerated here whether it is at all possible for your individual, regardless of which position that person occupies, can execute all these tasks and bear responsibility for all of them?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this is impossible.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, in this particular provision, Mr. Stojanovski, do you see anywhere where it says that the director of the public security bureau performs any functions?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that we mentioned that these are competencies within the ministry, not of persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And since you said that the minister heads the ministry, does this provision indicate which tasks and responsibilities the minister has?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sure you recall, Mr. Stojanovski, that in answering a question put to you by the Prosecutor on several occasions, you said that in addition to this particular provision, it is necessary to look at other rules of procedure, systemization, and so on and so forth; and you said that on page 9246 and 47 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Stojanovski, why did you insist on that, and why is it necessary in addition to this provision and Article to look at other by-laws and other rules governing systemization, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Things must be seen as a whole because the law gives the general competencies, the categories of persons, and the organisational units which carry out tasks. It lists the persons who carry out these tasks, their responsibilities, and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If we take a look at Article 12, for instance, you mentioned that Article earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English, it is on page 8965, ERN number, it's on page 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you worked in the crime police, in order to know what the crime police does of the work stipulated under Article 1, to what extent is it necessary to take into account Article 12 of this law as well, and then, also, the rules and regulations that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it is -- it is essential in order to establish properly the competencies and responsibilities, so as to know who does what, if I can say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'm sure you will recall that on a number of occasions, you said that -- or rather, you were saying what an authorised individual does and who these authorised individuals are, and you said that very often it was necessary to refer to Article 24 governing the Ministry of Interior. You said that on 9274 and 5 of the transcript. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let's take a look at that Article 24 which you pointed out to us. And as you said, and I'm not contesting that at all, this Article regulates who the authorised persons are. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, can you read out what it says in paragraph 2, under point 1, who the authorised officials are?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Authorised official in connection to this law are considered: Point 1, police and operative employees; 2..." --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just wait a moment, wait there a moment. When it says "authorised officials," does that indicate who conducts these operative affairs or does it just enumerate the persons concerned?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It gives a category of persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, when it says "police and operative employees," what do they do? What level of affairs are they engaged in?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are persons who directly carry out operative tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now read out point 2, please, of that same Article.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Employees who carry out activities that are in direct connection to police and operative activities."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So is my understanding correct if I say this is a category of employees in the ministry who have a connection to the operative employees who are in charge of the operative side of affairs?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This would be, for example, crime technique, police forensics.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now read out point 3, please.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The minister, his deputy, supervisors of certain organisational units."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, in point 3 there, the people or persons enumerated there, are they, in any way, or does that point, in any way, or indicate that these are individuals who are engaged in operative affairs from point 1, or are they linked to the operative affairs as stipulated in point 2?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, in connection with this Article, you always added and said that we should see what each authorised official does according to the rules governing systematization. So would you read the last paragraph of Article 24 now.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In the act for systemization of the posts within the ministry, the posts with special responsibilities and authorisations are defined in the sense of paragraph 2 of this Article."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, this provision of Article 24, does it confirm your testimony before this Court to the effect that an individual provision, especially paragraph 1 or point 1, cannot be viewed without the acts that you have just mentioned and read out from Article 24?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe I said --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, the witness has answered, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: He's commenced to answer, but I have interrupted him. I interrupted him because the question has gone to the ultimate, in asking a point of law of a factual witness, and I don't know what your objection may have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My objection was essentially the same, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I withdraw the question, Your Honour. Thank you. The witness has testified about that several times already, so there's no need for me to go into it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I just make the comment, Ms. Residovic. We've allowed you and, indeed, Mr. Saxon considerable liberty about evidence about particular provisions of laws, but the basic rule is that the law is for this Chamber not for witnesses to speak about, certainly not witnesses who claim no particular expertise in law, and this last question was just too far.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Well, I understand what you say, Your Honour, and that's why I retracted the question. But as this witness was intensively questioned during cross-examination about the different provisions, in my re-direct, Your Honour, I should like, nevertheless, to deal with certain legal provisions but I will take care not to go too far, as I have done on this occasion. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, tell me, please, all these authorised officials mentioned here, are they engaged in all the affairs, all the authorisations as provided for by this law?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are divided.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in that case, I'd like to you look at a document after tab 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is Exhibit P96.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is the rules. Look at the Macedonian side, 0424625.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the English version, it is -- I don't seem to have the English version. I apologise, Your Honour. Perhaps the witness isn't feeling well. I seem to see him --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, the Prosecutor discussed something with you, and you mentioned the provisions of Article 166 and 168. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that we discussed this and that I did not succeed to explain to him that he was implementing Articles for one situation, while these Articles pertain to an altogether different situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, Mr. Stojanovski, that this Article 167 that was mentioned, and when it was put to you, you said that they were quite separate situations, and you said that you were duty-bound to inform the legal organs only when asked by them to do so?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, based on your experience, Mr. Stojanovski, would the police call the prosecutor or send him information if it heard rumours or happened to read in the papers that a crime had allegedly been committed? Would that merit it?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would the police call the prosecutor or would write to the prosecutor if, during the course of a decision, for instance, it had heard that, allegedly, a crime had taken place?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a policeman working for many years in the police force, how many such rumours, information, and knowledge that -- does the police hear about during a week or a certain period of time?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: An enormous number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As the Prosecutor put it to you, if the police had to inform the prosecutor every single time faced with situations like this, when you, in fact, had no relevant information to prove that such an act had been committed, how much information would the prosecutor have to receive?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He probably would not be able to enter his office in such a case.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sure you recall, Mr. Stojanovski, that you said that the police first has to check out the rumours and to have sufficient grounds to believe that an act -- a crime had, in fact, been committed and that an act constituted a crime; and only once it has done that could it proceed to inform the prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor - and this is on page 9251 of the transcript - read out some Articles of the Criminal Code and the Rules of Service. Tell me, based on your own experience, do the police undertake certain measures provided for in these rules and regulations, so we don’t have to look at them again now, before they check out any information about an event and whether there are any grounds for suspicion, or is this done during another period of time?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the transcript in the English language. There is a condition, if you will, in this regard, a benchmark, and that is that there should be reasonable suspicions that a certain crime has been committed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, with respect to Ljuboten, you said, and we saw a document, that the prosecutor was informed about the death of Atulla Qaili. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also during the cross-examination, you said that you tried to verify the information that was coming into you that certain individuals were mistreated at check-points and in some police stations. Do you remember answering questions about that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I answered and I tried to do so on several occasions and in several ways.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, in the post you occupied in 2001 and 2002, after all the efforts that were made, did you have evidence or information which would constitute sufficient grounds to suspect that a policeman or the police had, indeed, mistreated those civilians or the people that it took into custody and brought into the police station?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, do you remember, Mr. Stojanovski, that the Prosecutor showed you a piece of information about the measures that the police took after the demonstrations in Skopje on the 9th of August, and which happened after the events in Karpalak? Now, do you remember that you looked at that document and discussed it with the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you also recall that on that occasion a part of a report was shown to you, in which it said that after an interview with a suspect, it was established that four more persons might have been the perpetrators of crimes - that was on page 9269 of the transcript - and those other persons were Brle, Cikoi, Marjan, and Igor. Do you remember discussing the document?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, when asked by the Prosecutor, you agreed and said that in addition to the information that you would receive from the injured party, you could also receive information from witnesses and suspects, and you said that on page 9270 of the transcript. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now to go back to questions related to your efforts concerning the events surrounding Ljuboten. Now information about this, if information to the effect that persons were mistreated at check-points and police stations, if they were truthful, if this information was truthful, then who would be the suspects? Who would be suspected of having committed those acts?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understand your question correctly, then it would be the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While checking out this information, did you at any point in time ask the chief of OVR Cair whether the police of OVR Cair at the check-points and in the police stations ever mistreated the people that had been taken in?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he ever tell you that the police mistreated anybody, had mistreated anybody at any check-point or at any police station?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Krstevski ever tell you that he personally watched any member of the reserve force in front of the police station at Cair abuse any persons?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During your efforts to check out the information and the rumours that reached you in various ways, to the effect that the police had overstepped its authorisation in the police stations, did you at any point in time discuss that with the police commanders, police chiefs of those police stations?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did any of those chief of -- chiefs of police confirm that information and provide you with any relevant evidence to the effect that a policeman, in a given police station, had, in fact, mistreated anyone, people who had been brought into the police station?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did any witness, a civilian, or anybody else who happened to be on the spot at the time provide you with any information, any relevant information, or any intimations from which you would be able to deduce in a sufficiently reliable manner that sufficient and reasonable grounds existed to suspect the police of having overstepped its authorisations?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have you, Mr. Stojanovski, considering that several times you stated that Ljube Krstevski was an experienced police officer, have you, in 2001 or 2002, any reasons to believe that Ljube Krstevski was not telling the truth about those facts?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any reason to mistrust any of the commanders of police stations that you asked about those issues?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no reason for this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you find the data on ill-treatment or any other overstepping of police powers in the documents that you yourself, as you stated, saw several times, or you requested to see them?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no such data.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, through this information, Official Notes, information notes, or orders related to the check-points, notice that it was an unusual way of reporting, or was it the customary manner of reporting pursuant to the rules of service?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything was usual.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: From the way in which the police stations reported and the OVR reported, were you able to deduce that something was wrong?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that everything was being carried out in a usual fashion.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, several times already you stated, and we also saw documents to that effect, that the injured parties did not want to discuss issues with the police. You also stated that nobody reported any event, any case of ill-treatment, that nobody informed you about the alleged ill-treatment, neither the injured parties nor the court. Do you remember having said that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, if there was no complaint from an injured party or anyone else who would have been aware of the unlawful conduct of the police, and if the potential perpetrators did not admit it or they did not indicate other potential perpetrators, if the alleged perpetrators hid from you the facts or if they lied to you about those facts, if the written documents did not indicate in any way that there was suspicion, could you, as a police officer, have a substantial way of establishing the facts corroborating the notion that the acts actually took place?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, having that fact in mind, were you able to undertake any other measures that were foreseen in those Articles that the Prosecutor showed you, Article 140 and 142 from the Law on Criminal Procedure and the Article 167 and 168 of the Rules on Performing Service in the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, you were also asked about Article 6 of the Law on Internal Affairs. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I remember well, you then stated that the minister is only able to issue his orders from within the remit of his competences. Did I understand that well?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I said.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the witness to pause before answering to allow the translation to be completed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will kindly ask you to look again at the Article 6.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the counsel to ask the witness to pause because the witness is not wearing any headset.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the screen --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The interpreters have asked us to ask you to pause before answering the question because you are not wearing the headset. You do understand me but you can't hear what the interpreters are saying. Very well. You have the Article 6 in front of you.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My apologies. I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is, again, Exhibit P86, paragraph 6, N000-8963.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We have Article 6 now. The law is in tab 2, so you can see it also from the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, does this Article speak about the duty of the minister at all?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is there anywhere in this Article where the powers, the competences of the minister are prescribed?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 2 of this Article, whose responsibility is stipulated?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the employee in the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, Mr. Stojanovski, who gives certain powers or competences to the minister?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The law, the government, the president of the Republic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move on to something else now. When asked by the Prosecutor, you stated that yourself and Mr. Bliznakovski were standing in for the head of sector for internal affairs, Skopje, Mr. Zoran Efremov. Do you remember, Mr. Stojanovski, did Mr. Efremov perform his duty in August 2001?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The fact that you were standing in for him during a certain period of time was clarified by you yesterday, but could you just say what was that period of time?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was at the beginning of 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, as far as I remember, you stated that he had been in a car accident and he was then absent from work. That was the reason for you standing in?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My learned colleague appears to be perhaps suggesting a different response to the witness. He has answered the question. I believe it was at the beginning of 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe, Your Honours, that I'm not leading the witness and not suggesting. At the end of yesterday's testimony, as far as I remember, but we will also find it now, the witness stated that that was at the end of 2000 or the beginning of 2001, and he mentioned the traffic accident. So that was on page 9335, line 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, Mr. Stojanovski, that the Prosecutor asked you to show the legal provision that prevented the minister or director from performing a duty; for instance, from ordering someone to investigate a crime? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I know that you stated several times that you were not a lawyer; but if you know, tell me, is the Law on Internal Affairs developed in a way that it establishes prohibitions.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of the law is not to establish prohibitions. There are other laws to that end. The goal is to regulate the competencies and authorisations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At one point in time, do you remember the Prosecutor asked you whether the minister was the highest officer in the MOI, in the Ministry of Interior. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, do you know whether the elected officials, that would mean ministers, so your minister of the interior included, are they employees of the Ministry of Interior, employees of the ministry at all?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're not employed at the ministry, rather at the government.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When asked by the Prosecutor, on page 9299, you answered: "Yes. I remember that conversation. Still, I can't remember from the list that you showed me, the one showing telephone conversations, whether that was a telephone call that went through a cell phone or a landline." Please, let's clarify this situation a bit further. Tell me, could you remember what was that conversation that you spoke about when you answered the Prosecutor's question in this way.

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: About the conversation I had with Mr. Krstevski in regards to the meeting with the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The Prosecutor also asked you about protecting the reputation of the police, but I would -- I prefer to ask you about facts. But this time I will ask you about your opinion. How do you -- as an officer who performed high duties in the police, what is your opinion? How could the reputation of the police be protected, safeguarded?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Above all, by lawful and professional performance of work tasks and duties; and if there are violations, that they should be processed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When performing your duties, did you have another treatment of a police officer who had perpetrated a crime when comparing to another individual that had perpetrated a crime?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the law does not provide us with such rights. The person who infringed the law has to be held responsible, whether this be a policeman or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovski, you said that when you were not able to verify certain information, the case could remain on stand-by in a police station or you could continue verifying, checking up some facts, even though the case is in the hands of the justice system bodies, although you don't have the duty any longer to do so. With regards to this case, Ljuboten, events in and around Ljuboten, tell me, do you believe that you closed that case, or was the case still open?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The case was not closed. I believe we mentioned, previously, there were exhumations, autopsies which were important for continuing the work on this case. However, we did not receive information or instructions by the public prosecutor or investigating judge, nor any kind of information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the final question, Mr. Stojanovski. At the beginning of your testimony, you stated that you came to tell the truth before this Court and that you knew what were the circumstances with regards to the Prosecutor's attitude towards you in which you were coming here. Tell me, you testified for quite a long time now, so tell me, when the Defence called you to testify, did you, at any moment, request any protective measures to be able to tell the truth before this Court?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How does this question arise out of cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe, Your Honours, that it does, because the questions I reacted at the end, if you remember, were precisely questions that the Prosecutor asked, accusing the witness of certain issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please continue, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Stojanovski, did you at any moment request that your testimony is not transparent; actually, did you request any protective measures to be able to tell the truth before this Court?

utterances.speaker: PETRE STOJANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Stojanovski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. I have concluded the examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Residovic. Mr. Stojanovski, that concludes the questioning for you in this case. We thank you for coming to The Hague and your assistance, and you will now be able to return to your ordinary activities. The court officer will show you out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to express my appreciation to the Court for the understanding it showed towards me, and I apologise for disrupting the usual order and schedule of the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber understands there is a procedural matter which is to be raised now. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the next witness we're calling will be shown a significant number of documents. However, one part of those documents that will be shown to the witness, eight documents in total, are still not on our 65 ter list. You know that we announced that. Considering the fact that we found some new documents after the submission of this list, we announced that we would ask that this list is amended. The Prosecutor also disclosed some new documents to us, and we will also ask that they are added to the list. I will kindly ask you, Your Honours, to be permitted to have these documents that are in the binders and that will be uploaded in the e-court to have them shown to the witness in the course of cross-examination [as interpreted]. The Prosecutor has already received all those documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just one point of clarification. If Ms. Residovic could clarify whether the Prosecution has also received English translations of each document or at least are available on e-court. Is that the situation?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The Prosecutor has received those, both Macedonian version and the translation, and all those documents are in the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you able to identify each document so that we know what we're talking about, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. That is 65 ter 1D1266. That is a committee deciding in the second instance on the -- upon the appeals against the decisions of the disciplinary body or the ministry. Then 65 ter 1D1267. That is rules of procedure before the second instance disciplinary committee. Then 65 ter 1D1268, which is the law on special rights of members of the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia, dated 15th of January 2002, published in the Official Gazette. Then 65 ter 1D1261 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 1D1271.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is a part of a disciplinary file that we received from the Prosecutor on the person Enver Guri. Then 65 ter 1D1272. Again, it's a part of that same disciplinary file on the person Enver Guri. Again, 65 ter 1D1273 and 65 ter 1274 are the same. So these four documents are parts of one discipline case, which pertained to this person, Enver Guri. Finally, 65 ter 1275. That is decision of the committee in the second instance. So we kindly ask you to allow us to include this in our 65 ter list dated 10 January 2008, and to allow us to be able to use them in the examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Leave will be given to amend the Rule 65 ter exhibit list to include those eight documents, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will now, I think, commence the next witness. Further to the comments made by the Chamber earlier, and given the nature that can be seen of some of the anticipated evidence of this next witness, the Chamber would make it clear that the questions of the Law of Macedonia will not be decided on the basis of evidence but on the interpretation an application of the law. Nevertheless, the Chamber will continue to allow some reasonable freedom of question about the general understanding of the application of the law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam. Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card which is given to you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness's microphone is not on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Ms. Dorevska.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, we've already met, but let me introduce myself officially. My name is Edina Residovic and together with my colleague, Guenael Mettraux, I am Defence counsel for Mr. Ljube Boskoski. I'm now going to ask you to give us your full name, your first and last name.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: My name is Vesna Dorevska.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before I move on to my questions, Ms. Dorevska, I'd like to inform you of something. You and I do not -- although we do not speak the same language, we do understand each other. However, my questions and your answers need to be interpreted for the Trial Chamber and everybody else in the courtroom to understand them, to know what I'm asking you and what you are answering. That is why I would like to ask you to make pauses between my questions and your answers to give the interpreters time to interpret. Have you understood?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Ms. Dorevska, tell me where and when you were born?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: I was born on the 15th of March, 1965, in the city of Caplijna in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, what education do you have?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: I have university education.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me where and when you completed your schooling?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: I graduated from the Faculty of Law at the Skopje University in 1989.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me when you started working and where.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: I started working in the district trade court. I was their volunteer for the duration of eight months; then, from the 10 of February 1992, as an apprentice within the sector of internal affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what status did you have when you got your job?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: At that time, my status was of an apprentice.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, after this period of apprenticeship, what work were you engaged in?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: After passing the apprentice exam in May 1992, I was given a contract for an independent human resources officer in the organisation and human resources department. In 1995, I was promoted into a chief officer on employment within the Ministry of Interior. In 1997, I was promoted into a head of section in that same department where I was working. In 1999, that same contract was extended, head of a section, but the status of the job was changed. That job became one with the status of an authorised officer. And after passing the professional vocational exam, I had again a contract for a section. In the year 2000, I was promoted into a head of the department for personnel affairs. In November 2001, I received a contract to be acting head of the department for personnel affairs. In March 2002, assistant to the minister in the sector for legal and personnel affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, let's just clarify something. The last thing you said. You first said that you were appointed as a leader in the legal and personnel department; and then, later on, in January, you were assistant minister of the sector for legal and personnel affairs. Are they different work posts?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: No, not at all. That is the same post.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, why were you given this appointment then, a different one?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Since at one point in time, the parliament of the Republic of Macedonia, after passing the law on civil servants, imposed an obligation for all managing posts in the state to have identical titles, to have the title of a head. There was a decree defining that, and the ministry acted upon that decree and changed the titles of the work posts. So that post, during the time when I became the acting, the provisional head, had the title of head of department for legal and personnel affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that how everybody else in the ministry working in the separate departments and on separate affairs, did they have to have the same appointments for the same work posts with different names, different titles?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course. That is part of the work of the ministry, in case of any amendments to the act for systemization. Regardless of whether the working duties are the same, the officer needs to have a new appointment, a new contract, if the job title changes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since we're on the subject, this title, head or leader, which was established on the basis of that law which was in force for a certain time, does it remain in force? Is it still applied?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: No. That title changed soon afterwards because the assessment was that those titles were not of benefit for the Ministry of Interior because the Law on Civil Servants, for the most part, does not apply to the officers within the ministry. And based on the assessment and consultations with the competent services in the state, we decided to that it would be most appropriate to restore the old titles that provide greater functionality to operation of the ministry, and we did it again through the amending of the act of systemization. The same applied to my job post. The old title was restored, assistant to the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, as you said, that this applied to the other heads of departments. In one of the departments, for example, of the Ministry of Interior, what was the title before, what were the titles applied to civil servants, and what is the law like today?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: These posts used to have corresponding job titles – chief of sector, chief of department of the interior. With the changes made, the posts received the title of heads – head of department of the interior, for example,- and then again the old titles were re-introduced - chief of department of the interior or chief of sector – depending on the organisational scheme in question. This means that several… that the people who occupied those posts received several decisions referring to one and the same post over a given period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Ms. Dorevska, for interrupting your flow with these explanations. You were talking about the tasks you were engaged in. Tell me what your job is today?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Today, I still hold the same post, assistant to the minister in the sector for legal and personnel affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what the competencies and authorisations of your particular sector? Can you explain that to us?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course. The sector primarily works in the area of regulations. It drafts the laws, secondary legislation in the area of internal affairs. It drafts acts on systemization an organisation. It works, and it did especially during that time, in the area of employment relations and the procedure from the moment of employment until the termination of the employment for the employees.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how your sector is organised in order to be able to carry out all the duties that you have just enumerated?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: There are two units: The unit for regulations and legal affairs and the unit for personnel affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to your regular education and the professional job -- your professional job, tell me, Ms. Dorevska, did you have, during your work, any additional professional training or education?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course. Throughout that entire period of six, ten years of effective work, I had continuous vocational training, seminars, additional educations in the area where I work.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us some of them; although, there are many courses that you seem to have attended?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course, most of them were in the area of human resources management and in the area of drafting regulation; but, of course, there were seminars and trainings related to management primarily. At any rate, there were many such seminars.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And where were those courses that you attended held mostly?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Most of them were held in the Republic of Macedonia. In the recent years, such seminars are organised abroad, but most of them were in our own state.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And can you tell us who the organisers of those courses were or seminars or vocational training that you attended?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Those trainings were organised by many national experts, but for the most part foreign representatives participated; foreign experts for the most part through Council of Europe, OSCE, European Commission. I can't remember precisely all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, we're now going to move on to another area. In view of your job and the kind work you did, I am going to ask you some questions with regard to the organisation and competences and the remitt of the Ministry of Interior in 2001. First, let me ask you this: Can you tell us which regulations governed the competencies of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course. The competence of the Ministry of Interior is regulated through several laws and regulations: First, the Law on Organisation and Work of the State Administration Bodies; then the Law on Government; the Law on Internal Affairs; secondary legislation enacted the by the Ministry of the Interior; and, to an extent, also the Constitution of the Republic of Macedonia also defines certain aspects relevant for the functioning of the ministries.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I understood you, you said that those were some of the laws. Now tell us how many laws in the Republic of Macedonia there are which relate to or define the competence and authority of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: There are several such laws that regulate the area of internal affairs; more than 20 laws at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you quote some of them, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course. Law on Security of Passenger Traffic, Law on Personal Documents, Law on Citizenship, Law on ID, Law on Residence and Dwelling, Law on Aliens, Law on Prevision of a State Border, Law on Weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the end of your previous answer, you mentioned the constitution as governing some of the competence and authority of the ministries. Now, Ms. Dorevska, I don't expect you to be a constitutional law expert. You are a lawyer nonetheless, and it is up to the Trial Chamber to determine and decide on the points of law. But could you, if you can, tell me what questions are contained in the constitution of Macedonia which would be relevant for the work of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: The constitution, above all, defines state administration. It speaks about bodies of the state administration, and the constitution lists that the regulation of the area of state administration will be regulated by special laws, systematic laws adopted with two thirds majority of overall MPs. Because the ministries, as part of the bodies of the state administration, are, in fact, bodies of the state administration, the constitution establishes that they're independent in carrying out their tasks and that they carry them out in accordance with the constitution and the laws.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Your Honours, in connection to that response, I would just like to indicate Exhibit P91 which is the constitution of Republic of Macedonia, and Articles 88, 89, 92, 95, and 96. Your Honours, I would now like to have the binders handed out, but I'm looking at the clock and perhaps this would be a good time to take a break, so that that could be done during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will have the first break now and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, a moment ago, you told us the basic provisions in the constitution governing the work of the state authorities, including the Ministry of Interior. Now, tell me, whether in keeping with your knowledge of the constitutional provisions, there are certain provisions which relate to the ministers of the state administration and by the same token the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course, the ministers are part of the government elected by the parliament. They're officials who have immunity and who for their work are accountable before the government.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether it is stipulated how the ministers are responsible to the bodies they're responsible to and to whom they are, indeed, responsible?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: The ministers are responsible before the government and the parliament which elects them; and the government, if dissatisfied with the work of the minister, can propose that that minister be dismissed from that office. And, of course, there's another institute, the one of impeachment, whereby -- which can be raised before the parliament, and then the parliament can decide upon the accountability of that person.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, with respect to that answer given by the witness, I'd like to draw your attention to Article 89 and 82 [as interpreted] of the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia. 89 and 92 are the Articles.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please take a look at the document to be found after tab 2 in the binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is Exhibit 551, P551; N002-5314, ERN number; page 1. Would you turn to the second page of that document; N002-5315 in the Macedonian version is the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, do you recognise the document?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course. This is the Law on the Government of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Stipulating the laws that are of importance to the ministries and minister, you mentioned the Law on Government of Macedonia as being one of them. Now tell us why you mentioned this law on the government and why would that law be important for the position of the ministry or minister?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: The Law on the Government is one of the important laws because it regulates the competencies and the work of the government. However, in the provisions, it also deals with the obligations of the minister; that is to say, of all ministers, not only of the Minister of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Under whose competence and authority or whose competence and authority is to see whether the laws are being implemented properly and other regulations that they're enforced?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: All minister is competent in his area to carry for the lawful execution of all provisions which are relevant to the area which he leads. The same applies to the Minister of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in what way does the government execute its functions in relation to the ministries?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: The government is a collective body, and the government in effect cares for the organisation of the work of all ministries. However, at the same time, the government supervises the work of the ministries. At the same time, as part of the government, there are a number of working bodies, commissions of the second instance, which in a way control the work or the decisions adopted by the ministries; for example, in my area, this is the first instance commission deciding upon labour relations laws, and there are several such commissions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Ms. Dorevska, can government give guidelines and instructions to a minister, what is the relationship, and how does the minister act in respect of these guidelines and instructions?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course, the government can't [as interpreted] give proposals and instructions for the work of the ministries and the minister through conclusions of the government which are obligatory and must be implemented.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: In line 32:22, "can give proposals."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: A moment ago, you said that, in the government, the government has various commissions. Now, what regulates this procedure; that is to say, the manner in which the government relies its function as a collective bodies, or rather, in what way do the ministers, as members of the government, act within the government?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: There are special rules for the work of the government which elaborates the provisions and the manner of work in a more detailed manner of all bodies which are formed within the government.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In relation to that answer by the witness, I would like to point out Exhibit P551; Article 5, 9, 12, 13, and Article 28 and 30 of the Law on Government; and Prosecution Exhibit P552, which are the Rules of Procedure for the Government of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like now to ask you, Ms. Dorevska, to take a look at a document to be found after tab 3, which is Exhibit P92. Have you found the document? It's on your screen as well.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. I see it in the binder and on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the document?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course. This is the Law on the Organisational of Work of Government Bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you enumerated the basic laws governing the organisation and competencies of the ministries, you mentioned this particular law as well. Now, why is the Law on the Organisation of Work of Government Bodies of importance to the work of the state organs and the Ministry of Interior as well?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: This Law on the Organisational and Work of Government Bodies, as I already mentioned, is set also in the constitution of Macedonia. This is a systematic law which regulates, as Article 1 stipulates, the organisation, authority, and work of the government bodies. This is one of the most important laws that determine the organisation of the ministries and their competencies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To what extent is this law a systematic one or basic law, an umbrella law, to be implemented by the ministries, including the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: This is obligatory for all ministries, including the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Among the basic laws, when you started your testimony, you said that the law governing the work of the Ministry of Interior was one of them. Now, what does that particular law regulate?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: The Law on Internal Affairs is lex specialis pertaining, and defining above all, the term "internal affairs," what the area of internal affairs entails, the organisation of the ministry, and many other issues which are related to internal affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that the Law on the Organisation and Work of the State Administration Bodies are -- was a systematic law, a comprehensive one, and that the Law on Internal Affairs, as you said, was a lex specialis, as you put it; so a special law linked to the Ministry of Interior in other words. Tell me, please, Ms. Dorevska, in case the Law on the Ministry of Interior is not dovetailed with certain provisions and not been harmonised with certain provisions subsequently adopted on the law governing the state administration, which law, to the best of your knowledge on the application of laws in the Republic of Macedonia, would apply in such a case?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: In such a case, the -- the most recent law would be applied, the law which defines organisation, and that would be the Law on Organisation and Work of Government Bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So we've just been discussing a number of laws which you said were basic laws as far as the organisation of the Ministry of Interior was concerned. Now, Ms. Dorevska, are these laws which were in force in 2001?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. These were laws which were in force in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to the laws, the competence and organisation of the ministry, is it prescribed and determined by any other binding acts as far as the ministry is concerned?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course. The organisation of the ministry is regulated also with by-laws and regulations. This is the Book of Rules on the Organisation of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you, Ms. Dorevska, now to take a look at a document found after tab 10.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is Exhibit 1D107. The Macedonian page is 1D4371, and the English page is 1D4392.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have you found that document?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, when you said a moment ago that this was a Book of Rules governing the organisation and work, do you recognise this document, the document before you, as being what you've just testified about?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. This is this document, the Book of Rules on the Organisation and Work of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If something is changed or amended in the structure of the competence and authority, what happens then? What's the procedure?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: If the organisation is changed in any of its parts, in any segment of the ministry, then it is obligatory to make changes in this Book of Rules as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which part of the ministry is in charge of preparing the drafts or pre-drafts for the acts and documents and the amendments and addendums?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: This is for legal and personnel affairs where I work.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And who passes these general acts governing the ministries?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: They are approved by the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When a general act has been passed and approved, can you tell me in what way its amendments are incorporated into it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Changes and amendments, if they're smaller in scope, are done in the same way that the act is passed, with changes and amendments to the act itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is there any other way in which this is done?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course. If we're dealing with larger changes to the act which can bring about confusion about the manner of the changes, in order to ensure clarity of the document, a new such document is passed. The same act, but it is passed as a new document, as a new act.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If for legal and technical reasons you decide to enact a new document or act, what happens to the previous one, the old one?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: In such a case, the old act is no longer in force, and this is acknowledged in the new act, which is passed with the number of the act which was previously passed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In a situation like that, Ms. Dorevska, does the act represent just a new act, a new document, and the previous state of affairs is changed or remains the same? For example, does the unit remain the same; or a particular body, does it remain the same, or does something change there, too, down the line?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Nothing changes in essence; only certain elements of the document, of the act, which should make it better in the terms of its application.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let's take a look at the next document which you'll find after tab 17.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is Exhibit P75. Number 4249 -- 4692, that's the Macedonian; and it's 42-4692; ERN 42-4695-ET is the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, you have before you a document of the Ministry of Interior, dated the 26th of June, 2001. Can you tell me what this is all about?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: This is a decision for establishing a "posebna" police unit at the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you take a look at the last page of that document now, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for having to refer to the translation, but it says here "for the formation of a special unit," and that's what the witness said: "special posebna." We discussed this previously, Your Honours, just to avoid any misunderstanding about what the witness is saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, to make matters clearer, tell me, please, in 2000, what special unit existed in the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: At that time, there was the Tigers special police unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And does this document speak about that unit?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: No. This is an altogether different unit. This is posebna unit of the police, while the Tigers are a special unit of the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now take a look at the provisions in Article 15 to be found on page 424695.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in the English, it is 4695-ET. It's on page 4, or the end of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can take a look at it in the document in front of you.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: It's fine. I see it both in the hard copy and on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It says here that: "With the coming into force of this decision, the validity of the decision on establishing a "posebna" police unit for performing specific tasks," and then the number, "dated the 2nd of June, 1993, ceases or is null and void." Tell me, please, Ms. Dorevska, a moment ago, you explained to us how a document is changed, is amended. Although this particular document is called a decision to establish a posebna police unit, does it govern the formation of the unit or does it apply to something else?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: No. This decision does not mean or imply the establishment of the posebna unit, because this was established a much -- a while back. Article -- point 15, which provides the regulations of this document, says that this is just a new decision that contains changes within, and this is why it is adopted as a new act, at which point the decision for such establishing in 1993 is no longer in effect, but it is the same unit in question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you now, Ms. Dorevska, go back a tab. So after tab 16 is the document that we'd like to look at next.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is Exhibit 1D57. 1D2283 is the page number in Macedonian, and 1D2285 is the English page number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is also a decision on the formation of the posebna unit; and a moment ago, you referred to Article 15 of the previous document where you said that another decision, dated back to 2003 [as interpreted], was null and void. Tell me, please, what does this decision represent? What is that about?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: This is a decision by which, in 1993, a posebna unit of the police to perform specific tasks was formed. This is a decision which became null and void with the adoption of the decision we spoke of previously.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you now take a look at page 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2284 is the number, and 2286 for the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Take a look at paragraph 15, or point 15. In paragraph 15, it says: "The entering into force of this decision, the decision strictly confidential, the number," et cetera, "of the 1st of March, 1991, is terminated." Now, in view of this provision, and as you explained to us earlier on, can you still us what type of decision this is? Although it says that it's a decision to establish a posebna unit, what is the nature of this decision?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: This is an identical situation as the one we discussed previously, which means that the unit existed with the decision of 1991. With the decision of 1993, again organisational changes were made, most probably as a result of which a new decision was adopted, and the one from 1991 was terminated.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, Ms. Dorevska, we have now seen two decisions; and as you have explained it to us, they represent certain amendments. For some legal and technical reasons, they were adopted as completely new documents, new acts. Now, tell me, was a posebna unit actually established based on either one of these two decisions?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: I presume that it was established with the decision of 1991, while all other decisions are a continuation, normative continuation of this unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd now like to ask to you take a look at a document that you'll find after tab 15.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is 1D66, page 1D2321; and in the English, it is 1D2324 -- no, 2407. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: A moment ago, Ms. Dorevska, you said that there were two ways in which documents were amended, and we had the example of the situation when a comprehensive document was being enacted, although, in fact, it was only a case of changes being made to that document and additions added to it. Now, tell us what this document that have you before you represents?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: This is an amendment to the Book of Rules for the Organisation and Work of the Ministry of Interior. These are changes of existing Book of Rules.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at the next page -- or rather, it's the first page of this document, 1D2322; and in English, it is 2408.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The document in front of you -- or rather, in what way does this document change the general act?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: By changing -- changes and amendments and by using new technical rules in this area. In this case, it is a matter of a change in the Book of Rules for the organisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, at the top of that document, we see that the document comes pursuant to Article 55, item 1, of the Law on Organisation and Work of the Bodies of the State Administration, as it says at the top there. Tell me, please, to whom does this Article, Article 55, refer to, of the Law on Organisation for the State Administration?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: The Article 55 pertains to all ministers, and it regulates actually the acts that ministers could issue during their term of office.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let us now look at another document, and it comes after tab 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is Exhibit P92.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like us to look at that Article, Article 55, which you've just mentioned and explained to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is to be found on 1905, that's the Macedonian page; and the English page is page 15.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In response to a question of mine earlier on, you said that the ministers, based on this act, bring in certain acts. Now, what ministers does Article 55 of this law refer to?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: The Article 55 pertains to all ministers in the government.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of this law, does it follow; and if so, which competencies and authority, as far as the ministers are concerned and including the minister of the interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: During their work, the ministers have the duty to enact acts, rules, instructions, plans, decisions, and other acts that are necessary for them to perform their duty, or actually for the ministry that they had to perform its duty, if they're authorised for it by the law.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Among these numerous acts - most of them are general in narrate, I assume - there are orders, too. Now, can the ministers, and by the same token the Minister of the Interior, issue orders; and if so, when can they do so?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course, the Article itself indicates the fact that the minister can issue orders, but only when there is an express authorisation granted by law or another regulation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, referring to the law governing the government, you said that it could provide instructions or guidelines to the ministries. Tell me now, please, in addition to the general provisions as to what a minister can do as minister of one of the state administrative bodies, as far as the minister is concerned, and including the Minister of the Interior, are there other acts which determine his functions and competence?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Naturally, there are other acts that are included in numerous other laws governing the area that the minister is in charge of; and whenever there are such authorisations, the minister does issue other acts as well, because the minister represents the ministry, signs acts in communication with other ministries.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now let's go back to the Law on the Ministry of Interior; and for that, let us take a look at the document which is to be found after tab 5?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is Exhibit P86. It is N000-8981.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document, Ms. Dorevska?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course. That is the law that we work with every day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, was this law in force in 2001?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, it was in force.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, were any of its provisions changed or amended to include the provisions of -- according to the provisions of some other law?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: During the time when this law was in force, the Law on Organisation and Operation of the Bodies of State Administration was enacted in 2000, and it foresaw the organisation of the ministry in another way. It foresaw two bodies within the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, let us look at Article 1 now of this Law on Internal Affairs. Tell me, what does Article 1 provide for?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: The Article 1 of the Law on Internal Affairs regulates the internal affairs, as the Article itself says: "Internal affairs, in the sense of this law, are the," and then they are enumerated.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember, Ms. Dorevska, how many employees did the Ministry of Interior have at that time?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
