utterances.text: In 2000/2001, I believe there were slightly more than 9.000.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And how many these days?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Today, it has some 12.000, or around some 12.000 officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The people working in the Ministry of Interior -- or rather, who is it who puts the provisions of Article 1 into practice?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: This is put into practice by the ministry through its organisational forms and through both bodies within it; that is, the public security and the intelligence and counter-intelligence bureau --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Security and counter-intelligence bureau.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is the security -- the security and counter-intelligence bureau, what is that, in the legal sense?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: In the legal sense, these are bodies within the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 2001, for instance, which provision regulated the fact that the Ministry of Interior should organise a public security and counter-intelligence bureau and department for security and counter-intelligence?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: The Law on Organisation and Operation of the Bodies of Civil Service of the year 2000, and later, in 2001, the Rule Book on Organisation of the Ministry of Interior was amended.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you now take a look at the next document to be found after tab 3?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As we saw a moment ago, it is Exhibit P92.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is the Law on the Organisation and Work of Government Bodies. From the title itself, we can see that the law was passed on the 21st of July, 2000. Is that the same law that you talked about and that you said was enacted in 2000?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. That is the law, and that was the first time that the bureau for public security was established as a body within or under the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let's take a look at Article 16 of that same law, which is to be found on page 9493.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the English, it is on page 4 of that law.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me what this provision provides for in this system of laws and the law governing the organisation of work of state administration and its bodies?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: This Article primarily regulates the competencies of the Ministry of Interior and what they are; and in the second paragraph already, it says that within the Ministry of Interior, there are the bureau for security and counter-intelligence and the bureau of public security.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, these bodies within the ministry, in what way are they performing the duties that they are established for?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: They are independent in the performance of the duties, in the area to cover which they're established, because they were established to cover two specific areas. The one is public security and the other is state security, and they're completely independent in the performance of their tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who heads those bodies within or under the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: The bodies within the Ministry of Interior are headed by directors.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And who appoints the director of the body within the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Upon a proposal of the Minister of the Interior, the director is appointed by the government.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And who dismisses the director of the body within the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course, the same principle applies: The body appointing is the body dismissing. At any rate, the minister of internal affairs, if they are not satisfied with the work of some of the directors, it could submit a proposal to the government elaborating the reasons for the dismissal.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me to whom is this director accountable? The director of the body within the ministry, to whom does he report?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: The director is primarily accountable to the minister, because he or she is part of the ministry, and is accountable to the government as well because they are appointed by the government. With regards to the bureau for security and counter-intelligence, there is another aspect where the parliament exercises the control over the work, which means that they are accountable to the parliament. There is a special committee dealing with that within the parliament.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, when discussing these two bodies within the Ministry of the Interior, if I understood you well, the directors are accountable to the minister and to the government, bearing in mind that the director of state security, or the UBK, is accountable also to the parliament. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you look now, please, at the document after tab 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit P86, and that is the Law on Internal Affairs. N000-8984 is the page that I would like to see. That is on the page 17. The English page is N000-8966.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: "Article 17," instead of "page 17."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The title of this paragraph is: "Provision over the work of the directorate or bureau." The Article 17 reads: "The parliament of the Republic of Macedonia is supervising the work of the bureau through the respective committee." "The committee" as the Article 18 reads, "is submitting a report to the parliament of the Republic of Macedonia about the -- about its work at least once a year." Tell me, when you were answering my question and you stated that the directorate or the bureau for security and counter-intelligence is accountable before the parliament as well, were you referring to these provisions of the law?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. It was exactly these provisions that I was referring at, which indicate that the parliament exercises the supervision over the work of directorate for security and counter-intelligence, and this is the way in which also the director of the bureau has the duty to grant access and to provide all the data from within his or her sphere of competence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Within this remit of responsibilities or accountability of the director to the government and to the minister, could a director of a body within the ministry be criminally liable? Could they be held criminally responsible if they perpetrate a criminal offence?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Naturally, as any other citizen.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And could a director of a body within a ministry be held disciplinary responsible?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: No disciplinary responsibility could be requested.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you clarify this? Why can't the director be held disciplinary reliable?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: The director is, in a way, an employee of the Ministry of Interior, but they are still an official appointed by the government; and the disciplinary procedure does not apply to elected and appointed official, primarily because disciplinary procedure means termination of employment for a certain person. The directors do not have their employment based in the same manner as the other employees; rather, they are appointed by the government, which means that the Minister of the Interior, and not only the Ministry of Interior but other ministers and other directors of bodies that exist, the minister could not impose such sanctions, termination of employment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, then, if the minister and the minister of the interior by the same token would not be satisfied with the way in which the director of the body within the ministry performs or enforces the law in the area for which they are responsible, what could a minister do?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: In that case, the director [as interpreted] could make a proposal to the government for the dismissal of the director.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look again at the document in tab 3. That is Law on Organisation and Work of the State Administration. I would like to ask you to look together at the Article 50, paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is N001-9505, the Macedonian version; while the English version is on page 14.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you find this Article?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, it's fine. I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have here the second paragraph of this Article 50, which reads: "The director of the body within the structure of a ministry is personally responsible for his work and for the work of the body that he manages to the government and to the minister." Is this, Ms. Dorevska, the provision that refers to the directors of the bodies within the Ministry of Interior as well?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. This provision applies to the directors of bodies within the Ministry of Interior as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is this the provision that prescribes the way in which the directors are responsible, as you testified already when answering my previous questions?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: I apologise. I did not understand your question well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. A moment ago, answering my question, you stated that the director is responsible to the minister and the government. I'm asking you whether this provision that we just read out is the provision that actually confirms your testimony; actually, where you giving your testimony about that responsibility that was regulated with the indicated provision.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, this is the provision.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly like to ask you now to look at the document in tab -- after tab 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is, again, Exhibit P86, Article 14. That is N000-8984.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This provision, as we can see, provides that the director is independent in the performance of the work of the directorate and is responsible to the minister and the government of the Republic of Macedonia for their work. Ms. Dorevska, is this, again, the provision you were relying upon when you spoke about the way in which the directors of a bodies within the ministry are performing their duties and tasks?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, but please bear in mind that this provision refers to the director of the bureau for security and counter-intelligence. At that time, it was directorate for security and counter-intelligence, since that body within the ministry was established before the bureau for public security. So this is why the Law on Internal Affairs contains provision that are specifically referring to the work of this director.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When another body was established within the Ministry of Interior, was the position of both of those bodies identical or were there any difference with regards to the responsibilities within the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: The responsibility was completely identical. There was no difference, there is no difference between the responsibilities of both those directs. They are both independent. They are both accountable before the minister and before the government for their work.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to the law and the provisions that we just saw, tell me, Ms. Dorevska, are there any other acts of the ministry providing the competences of the bodies within the ministry specifying the competences of the bureau for security and counter-intelligence and the bureau of public security?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course, there are special regulations, secondary legislations, that prescribe the operation of those bodies. That is the rule book on performance of the works of the bureau of public security governing the area of public security, and rule book for performing tasks in the area of state security.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will kindly ask you now to look at the document in tab 9.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is 65 ter 1D1200. That is page 1D9674.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, tell me, at the bottom there of the page, we see that the Minister of the Interior enacted the rule book for conducting the work of the security and counter-intelligence directorate. Are you familiar with this document, Ms. Dorevska?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know when was this document enacted?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: It was enacted in 1998 because that was the time when the bureau existed as a separate body within the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will kindly ask you now to look at the document after tab 10.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit 1D107, and I would like to look at the page 1D4372. The English page is 1D4393.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You're familiar with this document, Ms. Dorevska?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course. This is the Book of Rules on the Organisation and Work of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When was the bureau for public security established, the one that is mentioned in Article 2, paragraph 3?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: The bureau exists as of 2000, when the Law on the Organisation and Work of Government Bodies was adopted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And could you tell me from when was that Law on Organisation and Work of Government Bodies in force?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: It came into force immediately when it was published in the Official Gazette. I cannot exactly remember the date in 2000. Probably, it was the seventh or eighth month. It was July or August.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Considering that you stated a moment ago that this new law being new and systematic organic law entered into force immediately, tell me, are you aware that then the director of the other body within the Ministry of Interior was appointed; and if you are, well, tell us, please, who was it and when did this take place?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: I believe that this was in August 2000. Then the first director of the bureau for public security was appointed. This was Mr. Zvonko Kasirski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know who, Ms. Dorevska, who was the director for public security bureau during the summer of 2001 and in 2002?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course, this was Mr. Goran Mitevski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And who elected Mr. Kasirski and Mr. Mitevski for the post of director of the public security bureau within the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: The government of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let's now take a look at the next document which is the one to be found after tab 11?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is Exhibit 1D105. 4261 of the English -- of the Macedonian version, and 4475 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the bottom of the Macedonian version, it says: "Resolution or decision for the appointment of a director of the public security bureau." So, tell me now, please, does this document show or confirm what you said, that in the summer of 2001, the director of the public security bureau was Goran Mitevski and that that appointment was made by the government?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. This document confirms that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the next document after tab 12.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is Exhibit 1D106 on page 2305 in Macedonian; and in English, 2306.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, would you now take a look at what it says there in the document I've just mentioned; and in view of your position in 2001 and 2002, tell me whether this document reflects the position or post of the director of the public safety bureau as it was in 2001 and 2002?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, this is exactly so. This document reflects the position of the director, to who appoints and dismisses him, and to whom he is accountable for his work.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour. I didn't want to interrupt the response of the witness, but I do note that this document appears to come from a -- the MOI web site. It is undated and it has absolutely no reference to any particular law or regulation and, therefore, the reliability of the document is in question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Issa. Ms. Residovic, I think you should attempt to obtain some verification, perhaps from the witness, of the authenticity of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that's why I asked the witness. She deals in legal matters, so I wanted her to tell us whether the contents of document corresponds to the position and post that the director for public safety occupied in 2001 and 2002. The witness at that time was the assistant to the ministry for legal affairs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The problem which is raised in the objection is that there is no apparent authenticity about this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this document is one of the exhibits. Now, in view of its authenticity -- or rather, you'll decide what weight you're going to give to the document, because at this point if time we can't provide any additional information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't believe that this document is an exhibit. I think it's a 65 ter -- it's on the 65 ter list, but it has not been admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's an exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you have the exhibit number, Ms. Residovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D106. It's from an official web site. We explained that at the time when you admitted this document as an exhibit. A number of Prosecution witnesses have commented on the document when it was presented to them: Risto Galevski, some others; and perhaps Jovanovski, I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just a moment. The witness, Ms. Residovic, may be able to confirm that this document taken from a web site is, in fact, a correct production of the position at the time and is a reliable document, and I think that will be enough to overcome Ms. Issa's concern.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Dorevska, you've just heard the suggestion made by the Presiding Judge. Tell me, please, can you tell the Court where this document comes from?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: This document is from the web page of the Ministry of Interior; and, of course, it represents the position of the director at that period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'd now like to ask you, once again, to go back to a document we've already seen. It comes after tab 10.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is Exhibit 1D107, the Book of Rules on the Organisation and Work of the Ministry of Interior. May we take a look at page 2 of this document. 4372 is the page number in Macedonian, and 1D4393 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, in Article 2, paragraph 3, it also says that the public security bureau, as a body under the ministry, is managed by a director. So does this provision also confirm what you testified about, about the position of the director of the bodies within the framework of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course. This provision confirms what I already said about the work of the director of the public security bureau.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, in general terms, what this Book of Rules determines?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: This Book of Rules regulates the internal organisation of the Ministry of Interior and the organisation of the bureau for public security.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that time - and we're talking about 2001 - can you tell me what bodies of the ministry were within the composition of the public security bureau, public safety bureau?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: These were the units of police, the unit of crime police, and several independent organisational units which carried out professional tasks for the unit of the police and the unit of the crime police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In explaining your answer to my question, when I asked you who implemented the tasks of the interior as -- as stipulated in Article 1, you said it was the different bodies and so on. Now tell me, in that regard, looking at Article 1 of the law, which duties were implemented by the public safety bureau as a body under the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: These were operative works, works which are as listed here, the place to maintain public law and order, control road and traffic, crime police. This includes the criminal procedure, prosecuting perpetrators of crime, everything that includes operative tasks as part of the work of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to the organisation of the bureau and the crime police department and some other independent bodies that you mentioned, tell me whether this Book of Rules regulates anything else, in connection to the public safety bureau or any other independent body within the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: In addition to the organisation relating to the bureau for public safety, this Book of Rules also regulates or defines the existence of other organisational units. These are units which carry out specialised tasks for the needs of the bureau for public safety and for the bureau for security and counter-intelligence which are functionally linked to the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you now take a look at Article 7 of this Book of Rules which is page 4377, and page 1D4399 of the English. Ms. Dorevska, tell me, now, please, whether this Article enumerates the organisational forms which you just mentioned and which were performed -- and which performed professional work for the public safety bureau and the security and counter-intelligence?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. These are such organisational units.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, the sector you worked in at the time and of which you are the head today, what part of the organisational structure of the ministry does that belong to?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: The sector for legal and personnel affairs, then and now, is an organisational unit which performs specialised -- specialised tasks for both units and is linked to the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, in view of your experience from that time and your professional knowledge and involvement in affairs of this kind, tell me, please, in 2001, and indeed in 2002, was there any kind of decentralisation or regionalisation of the Ministry of Interior; and if so, if it existed, what did it mean in terms of executing the tasks and accountability and responsibility for executing those tasks?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course, at that period of time, there were regional police services, regional organisational units, which are regulated by this Book of Rules. Then there were 11 such organisational units, which were established to carry out matters of internal affairs on the territory of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let's now take a look at Article 8 of this same document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is to be found on page 4379, Article 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It says here, in Article 8, that: "For conducting internal affairs on the territory of the Republic of Macedonia, the following regional organisational forms or units of ministry are established," and we have 11 sectors listed as you've just told us. Tell me now, please, bearing in mind Article 1 of the law that we discussed at the beginning of your testimony, where are the affairs, listed in that Article, carried out?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Works, as per Article 1, are conducted in specific organisational units, including the sectors for internal affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In what way are these affairs executed within the sectors?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: They have a certain independence in carrying out their work obligations; but within each sector, there are a number of other organisational units, the so-called units of internal affairs, in the police stations, and through them the sector of internal affairs carries out the affairs which are part of its competency on that given territory.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the operative execution of the affairs, in what part of the ministry are the affairs conducted in the operative sense?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: They're operatively carried out as part of the bureau for public security as part of the work of the crime police and the units for police, and with -- as part of the work of the unit of internal affairs, OVRs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When it comes to implementing the tasks within the sectors, in what way are these affairs conducted; that is to say, the internal affairs? Is it the sector that puts them into practice or are there any other bodies within the sector?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course, within the sectors, there are other organisational units which are operative and which carry out matters related to internal affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'd now like to ask you to take a look at a diagram or schematic attached to these rules?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And it's found on page 1D4390. And in the English, it is 1D4414.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of your testimony so far, does this diagram of the public safety bureau reflect what you know about it, what you know about the bodies that -- that made up the public safety bureau, and where internal affairs were conducted in an independent and autonomous manner?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. This is this scheme about which I was speaking about. These are the organisational units.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me where in this diagram we see those organs, those bodies?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: I apologise, which bodies do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The different parts making up the public safety bureau.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: In the public safety bureau is the unit of the crime police and the unit of police or department of police. Each of these units, departments, have organisational units of, and in the middle are the organisational units which carry out specialised tasks for these two units.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, outside this black rectangle, which is the public safety bureau with the department of crime police and the department of the police and the various other subsections catering to both these departments, we also see some separate organisational units. Tell me now, please, what are these other boxes? What do they represent, the other departments? It says special tasks unit, Tigers, and then a set of boxes. Your department is listed there, too, for legal affairs, sector for legal affairs. What is the basic task of these other units.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: These are specialised professional services which are functionally linked to the Minister of the Interior. However, the work which they carry out relates both to the bureau for public safety and for the bureau of security and counter-intelligence. This is my explanation also vis-a-vis the sector which I had. The sector for legal and personnel affairs is a professional service located in this part of the diagram but carries out professional services and specialised services for the whole ministry and the two units that are part of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, is this a good time to take the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will have the -- Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm very, very sorry to interrupt, simply that I was notified of a possible translation mistake; and before it escapes us, I just wanted to bring it to everyone's attention. At page 48, line 16 of the transcript, there's a sentence that reads: "The director could make a proposal to the government for the dismissal of the director." And the Prosecution assumes that that's perhaps just a simple translation error and the witness probably said "the minister could make a proposal."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sure that will be considered over the break by Ms. Residovic; and if she has no difficulty, nothing more will be said about it. But if there is a concern, it can be raised. We will resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, do you still have this diagram before you?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, I have it in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will kindly ask to you turn to the following page.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is 1D4391. The English page is 1D4415.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Answering my previous questions, you stated that on the territory of the Republic of Macedonia, regional organisational units or forms were organised to carry out the tasks within the area of internal affairs. Tell me, when you look now at this diagram, does this diagram corroborates your testimony about the regional organisational forms of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. This diagram confirms the organisation of regional organisational units.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If we look now at the first part of this diagram, where you read "SVR Skopje," there are some five boxes below. What do they represent?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: These are the five departments of internal affairs, organisational units, part of the sector for internal affairs, Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you were speaking about the carrying out of the operative tasks within the area of internal affairs, what were or what are the tasks of bodies of internal affairs that are carried out within the departments for internal affairs, OVRs?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Here, operative functions are carried out. This means tasks related to the crime police and matters related to the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Ms. Dorevska, did this rule book, in any way, deal with the issue of responsibility of officers of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course, this Book of Rules contains provisions which relate to the responsibility of the employees. Each employee is responsible for carrying out the obligations charged to his post, or her post; and for his work, he or she is accountable to his superior, direct superior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will kindly ask you now to look again to page 1D4388 of this same rule book, Articles 22 and 23.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D4411 is the version in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if we look at Article 22, it establishes, in the second paragraph, that the officers are responsible to their immediate superior and to the head of the organisational form to which they belong for the correct or proper execution of their works and tasks. Tell me, when you answered my question now about the responsibility, does this Article correspond to your understanding of the responsibility as it was established in the ministry in 2001?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. This corresponds to what I already said about the responsibility of the employees.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stated, previously, that if something would be changed in the structure and in the position of a given part of the ministry, then that rule book needs to be amended. Tell me, does this same principle apply to this rule book?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. The same principle applies to this Book of Rules as well, because this is a by-law of the ministry and a regulation which is subject to the same rules.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please now look at the document after tab 15.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit 1D66, 1D2321; and the English version is 1D2407.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, this is the rule book that we reviewed earlier, as well, when you were speaking about the principle, according to which the acts enacted by the minister are amended. I kindly ask you now to look at the following page in this rule book. Let's see how is this implemented and in accordance with your testimony; that is, it was necessary to amend the rule book if something changes with regards to the structure and responsibilities of the body.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is page 1D2322 and 1D4208.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering the contents of this rule book, tell me, what has changed with regards to the organisation of the Ministry of Internal Affairs through this amendment here?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: With these amendments to the Book of Rules, an organisational change was introduced. One organisational unit, in this case the unit for special tasks, Tigers, which previously was part of the organisational forms directly and functionally linked to the minister and carried out tasks both for the bureau and for the bureau for public safety and counter-intelligence, is now changing its position and is being transferred into the unit of the police of the section of the police as an independent organisational unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you kindly look now at the second page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is 2409 in English, and 2285 -- 2323 in Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Here we have, again, a diagram, organisational diagram. Tell me, is this change that we saw in the rule book reflected in this diagram as well?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. With the amendments to the Book of Rules and since the diagram is part of the Book of Rules, this is also reflected in the diagram, and we can see that the section for special tasks, Tigers, is becoming an organisational unit section in the unit of the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And who is now the superior the responsible officer for this unit.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: In this case, the position changes. The unit is no longer functionally linked to the minister, and the superior of the units for special tasks, Tigers, in this case is the under-secretary of the section of the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let move on to another topic now. Ms. Dorevska, are you familiar with the notion of "authorised officer"?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course. I'm aware of this term.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will kindly ask to you now look at the document after tab 5, and that is the Law on Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit P86 and Article 24. It is on page N000-8986, and the English page is N000-8967.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Ms. Dorevska, is this the Article which is the legal basis establishing who are authorised officers?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. This is a legal provision which establishes and defines the term "authorised person."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you comment on this line 1 of the second paragraph, which says that authorised officers, in terms of this law, are the employees of the police and operative employees. Who are those officers indicated here?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Authorised officers, in the context of this law, are considered under point 1, police and operative employees. These are person who is work in uniform; then operative employees, persons who work in the crime police; then employees who carry out activities that are in direct connection to police and operative activities. These are the other organisational units, such as organisational unit where I also work, because they are connected with the operative employees and the minister, his deputy, supervisors of certain organisational units, which, by force of law, are authorised officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this paragraph 3 that you just commented upon, the minister, his deputy, can you see from that any link from the minister to the operative employees, actually to the police that is the direct performer of the tasks, as you stated? You, performing your duties, are also linked, in a way, as it is stated in line 2. So to put it briefly, does this provision indicate that there some operative tasks of -- for persons indicated in line 3?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: No, not at all. It does not point to an operative function. Minister and his deputies are officials. They are not operative employees.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, with regards to the officers --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: To the competencies of authorised officers...

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: ... where are they regulated, and what are all provisions where they are regulated?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: These authorisations are regulated in by-laws. This is the Book of Rules on Organisation and for Systematisation of Workplaces. The Book of Rules on Organisation defines the organisational forms and the operative functions which they carry out; while the Book of Rules on Systemization of Work Posts lists exactly who -- which work posts or employees carry out operative functions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to what you stated, that the rule book on performing of tasks is the act establishing the competencies of the authorised officer, would you now please look at the document after tab 32.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit P96, and I would kindly ask -- that is the rule book for performing of tasks of the Ministry of Interior. Let's look at the page R042 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel kindly repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] R042-4623-03. Your Honours, I believe that we have already discussed this document. We are awaiting for the revised translation of the entire document. So the translation we have here is still a draft translation, and we requested that it be amended. So we will receive the revised document soon, the CLSS informed us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will kindly ask you, Ms. Dorevska, to look at the contents. Let look at the provisions number 2, application of special duties of authorised officers. It indicates here: Asking for ID; warning; summoning orders; referral to investigating judge and holding persons until the judge arrives; gathering of necessary information; detaining, bringing persons in; deprival of liberty; escorting people; entry and search of homes and other premises; search of persons; examination of vehicles, passengers, luggage, facilities, and premises; application of special means and methods in performing works; directing movements within a given area; restricting movements within a given facility or space; raid; ambush; roadblocks. Ms. Dorevska, are these mainly the competences that an authorised officer -- that an authorised officer could perform?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: These are the authorisations which can be applied by authorised officers if it is established in the act for the Book of Organisation, that this is part of their work tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, with regards to this, let me ask you another question. Does every, any authorised officer perform all these competences that we have just enumerated and others that are prescribed by this law?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: No, not all authorised officers have all of these authorisations. Authorised officers can have authorisations which are exclusively given to them as a task, which means that this Book of Rules enumerates all such authorisations. However, they can be separated between various organisational units in the ministry which carry out operative functions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is the delineation of this competences, what is the remit of the competences that an authorised officer has?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: This is regulated with the Book of Rules on Organisation which defines the authorisations of concrete and specific organisational units and, in particular, the Book of Rules on systemization of work posts.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As an assistant to the minister for legal and personnel affairs, are you an authorised officer?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. I have the status of authorised officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you search someone's residence?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course, that I could not do. So this is not part of my duties which I carry out on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In Article 24, we see that the minister is an authorised officer as well. Ms. Dorevska, does it mean, pursuant to this regulation and in accordance with the practice, that the minister can have the duties and authorisation to perform every and any competences that we enumerated a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: The minister does not have police authorisations at all. As I said previously, he is an official, elected and appointed official, which -- who does not have an operative function, which means that, by the force of law, he has the status of an authorised official but he or she cannot apply police authorisations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Reading the Article 55 from the Law on Organisation of State Administration, the organic law, we saw that the ministers, so by that token the Minister of the Interior as well, can issue orders. Can the Minister of the Interior issue orders; and if they can do so, when can they do so?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course. The Minister of the Interior, as well as other ministers, can issue orders. However, this can be done by the minister only when he is authorised to do so by law or by another regulation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If the minister has, as you stated, on the basis of law or another regulation, authorisation to issue an order, how must that order be treated by the employees in the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: In this case, they're obliged to carry out the order of the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will kindly ask you now to look again at the document after tab 5, Exhibit P86. That is the Law on Internal Affairs, and let's look immediately at Article 6 of this law.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] N000-8963 is the English page, while the Macedonian page is N000-8982.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the first paragraph of Article 6, it is stated: "The employees of the ministry are performing their duties and tasks in accordance with the rights, obligations, and authorisations determined by the law and other regulations that are brought based on the law." The second paragraph says: "An employee of the ministry must enforce the orders of the minister or a person authorised by him given in connection with the functioning of the ministry, except when the performance of the orders represents a criminal offence." Ms. Dorevska, answering my question, you stated that the employee has the duty to enforce -- to follow the order of the minister. Were you referring or is the basis for this testimony this provision from the law?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. What I said is grounded in Article 6 on the law of internal affairs which points to the duty of the employees in the ministry to carry out the orders of the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, this Article, does it regulate, in any way whatsoever, the duties and authorities of the minister?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: No. This Article does not speak at all about the duties and authorisation of the minister. It speaks of the obligations, the duties of the employees, in the case when a minister issues them a certain order.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when can the minister issue an order which an employee must carry out?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Always when he is authorised by law or by another regulation to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While we're discussing the minister, Ms. Dorevska, could you tell me what responsibilities the minister has, in keeping with your knowledge and the regulations of the Republic of Macedonia and in practical terms, because you worked for many years in a department linked to the minister?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: The minister is generally responsible for the laws and efficient application of the work and implementation in the sphere for which he is responsible; in case, the Minister of the Interior, he cares for efficient implementation and enforcement of the laws and all other regulations which are under the responsibility of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Ms. Dorevska, in what way does the minister head the ministry or manage the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: The minister manages, as is listed in the Book of Rules, by holding collegia, which can be in a broader or a more narrow composition; and in this way, he follows, so to say, the work, the situation, in the ministry which he heads.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In respect of the position of the minister within the ministry, tell me, please, since you said that he was elected by parliament and appointed in that way, is he accountable to parliament for his work?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course, the minister is accountable to the parliament for his work.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Earlier on, you said that the minister is bound by the provisions of the law, stipulating his authorisations and, of course, government -- he is guided by government decisions and decisions made by parliament or the "sobranje." Now, tell me, apart from those acts, that is to say, the laws or acts of organs to whom the minister is accountable and responsible, can the minister set his own tasks and assign duties himself, duties that are not specified by the law we mentioned and the provisions you talked to us about earlier?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: No. The minister cannot himself assign duties. His authorisations are specifically listed in the legal -- in laws and in by-laws.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We've spoken about what the minister can do if a director fails to carry out his duties within the department for which he has been elected, one of the bodies of the ministry. Now, can the minister take the place of a director and carry out his functions and responsibilities?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course, he cannot do this. These are different work positions, work posts.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can the minister, for instance, go on the ground, in the field, in an operative department of the crime-investigation police and conduct investigations or tell people how they should do their job when they are performing their duties as prescribed by the law?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: No. The minister does not have such authorisation, and he cannot do this in such a way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge and your practical experience, if, within the ministry, things are not going well, if the tasks are not implemented properly, and if the organisation is not bearing fruit and coming up with results, what can the minister do in cases like that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: He can undertake measures to submit a proposal if this pertains to the failure to -- of directors to perform duties. We said that he can submit a proposal forever their dismissal, he can change the organisation, he can change the systemization, he can adopt decisions for redeployment of people in various work posts.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And all those things that you have just enumerated, are they based on his own personal will or does he have the authorisation to do so under the law and the legal provisions?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: For all of these activities which I listed, they are authorisations in the law and a procedure which -- by which all of this can be done.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, do you know whether there are any legal provisions which give the minister direct orders for him -- or rather, give him the leeway to issue direct orders or take any other steps or measures if the situation requires?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I know such a provision. Perhaps, there is one such provision in the 20-odd laws which I mentioned perhaps in terms of road safety or something to that extent; but, specifically, I could not say.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, when the minister has a certain duty or authorisation under the law, prescribed by law, can the minister in that case and in conformity with what you know about the law in Macedonia and on the basis of your practical experience, can the minister convey his authorisation to other persons?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Of course, he can. If he has the original authorisations, powers, he could convey those to other persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the next document. It comes after tab 13.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is Exhibit 1D44. 1722 in the Macedonian, and page 1723 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We have before us a document which the commander of the special unit, Tigers, Goran Zdravkovksi, sent the Minister of the Interior, and the date is the 19th of July, 2001. If we recall the diagram we were looking at a moment ago, this special unit was linked to the minister, right? Is my understanding of that correct?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, it says here that, by an act of 1992, this special task unit was directly commanded by the Minister of the Interior and that means that the commander of the unit receives orders and tasks directly from the minister. Because the minister has assigned certain authority to the head of the department for police, the commander of the unit for special tasks receives orders and tasks also from the head. Tell me, please, Ms. Dorevska, does this document confirm precisely what you said an amount ago, when you were saying that the minister, when he has direct authorisation, can delegate that authorisation to another person and, in this case, it was the head of the police department that he was delegating that authorisation to?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes, it works like that. When the minister has authorisations vested in him by some act, he could delegate those to another person; and you can see from this document that this was done, that the authorisations were delegated to the head of the police department.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: A moment ago, we saw some rules about amendments and supplements to the work of the Ministry of Interior, dated August 2001, in which this special task unit, Tiger, was transferred to the police department. Now, tell me, at the point in time, when this unit was moved from under the authorisation of the minister to the police department, did the minister retain his authorisations to issue orders to the -- this particular unit, the Tigers, or Tiger?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: No. From the moment the act for systemization was amended, all authorisations with regards to powers were transferred to the head of the police department or the under-secretary in the police department, and the minister is no longer functionally linked to the unit, Tigers, and could not manage it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In that same diagram, the one we were looking at a moment ago, where the special task unit, Tiger, from August 2001 moved to the police department, who makes up the department, the police department?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: The police department consists of several autonomous organisational units.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are they the employees of the Ministry of Interior who perform their duties in civilian clothes, are they plain clothes men, or is it some other category of staff employed by the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Those are officers who perform their tasks while wearing uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, as you said, they come under the police department; they are members of the police department, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: Yes. They are within the police department.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, when this special task unit, the Tiger, was transferred, and I'm referring to the uniformed police as a whole, who has duties and authorisations over that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: First, those who head the organisational form. In this case, this is the Tiger commander; and, of course, the head of the police department.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What about the minister? Does he have any authorisations or duties or operational duties for him to be able to command the uniformed police?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA
utterances.text: No. The minister does not have operative duties with regards to command over the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'd like to move on to another area. Now, do you want me to make use of the few remaining minutes that we have, or could we perhaps adjourn?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I take it from your indication that it would be more efficient if we pause now. Very well. We will adjourn for the day and resume tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 15th of February, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.42 p.m.,
